title: Optimising Medical Nutrition in Chronic Kidney Disease and Kidney Failure
content:
Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is accompanied by progressive metabolic and clinical disturbances that can compromise nutritional status and impair physical function. Protein-energy wasting (PEW) is a frequent complication, arising from the interplay between inadequate nutrient intake and disease-related disturbances in protein and energy metabolism. As CKD progresses, medical nutrition therapy (MNT)  plays an increasingly important role in addressing evolving nutritional requirements and adapting dietary strategies to the patient's clinical condition, particularly during the transition to dialysis.

This narrative review discusses MNT across the CKD trajectory, with particular emphasis on its indications, implementation and monitoring. It addresses the nutritional disturbances associated with CKD and the role of nutritional support when dietary counselling alone is insufficient. Food-based strategies, dietary fortification, ketoanalogue supplementation, oral nutritional supplements and intradialytic parenteral nutrition are considered in relation to the specific nutritional deficits and clinical circumstances of patients. Particular attention is given to the transition to dialysis and the potential role of individualized nutritional prescriptions in patients receiving incremental hemodialysis. Clinical cases illustrate the application of these strategies in different settings.

Overall, the review highlights the need to adapt MNT to the changing nutritional requirements and clinical circumstances of patients throughout the CKD trajectory. However, evidence remains limited in several areas, particularly during the transition to dialysis and regarding the effects of nutritional interventions on functional and clinical outcomes. Further research is needed to establish effective individualized strategies and strengthen the evidence base for nutritional care across the CKD trajectory.
